Delivery Hero stock gains regulatory lift for Uber's Glovo deal
sum: Delivery Hero's takeover story gained regulatory momentum during the week after Ukraine approved Uber's proposed indirect control of the Glovo business in the country. The decision was reported on Friday, November 6, by The Kyiv Independent.

Ukraine's Antimonopoly Committee approved Uber's acquisition of indirect control through Uber International Technologies II Corporation. The approval covers Delivery Hero's Ukrainian Glovo operations, while other regulatory approvals and closing conditions remain outstanding.

The broader transaction would give Uber control of Delivery Hero businesses in 50 markets. Uber's offer period ended on Thursday, November 5, and the takeover is expected to close in the second half of 2027, according to the report.

A separate voting-rights filing released on Friday showed JPMorgan Chase & Co. with a combined 5.65 percent position in Delivery Hero. The position consisted of 3.11 percent in voting rights attached to shares and 2.54 percent through financial instruments, compared with 4.71 percent in the previous notification. The Delivery Hero voting-rights announcement said the threshold was crossed on October 29.

Delivery Hero stock traded at 36.90 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:38 CET on Saturday, November 7, 2026, 0.27 percent below the Xetra close of Friday, November 6, at 37.00 euros. Over the week, the Xetra close declined 0.80 percent from 37.30 euros on Friday, October 30.

Investors are weighing regulatory progress against the remaining conditions for the Uber transaction. The offer price and the timetable remain central reference points for the share's valuation, but neither the regulatory decision nor the voting-rights filing establishes a completion date.
Investors can follow the real-time quote of Delivery Hero stock for further trading updates.

Uber shares one number to tell everyone, how 'unpopular' AI Agents may be on its platform
sum: Tech giants and venture capitalists have spent billions hyping the rise of autonomous personal AI agents. They are selling or rather promising a future where software handles everyday tasks like hailing rides and ordering food. But it seems that in the real-world, consumers are still tapping their own screens. During Uber’s third-quarter earnings call, executives disclosed that only four rides worldwide were hailed via an AI agent during the week of Halloween — traditionally regarded as the company’s busiest week of the year.

Deliveries through Uber Eats saw slightly more activity, but the numbers remained negligible. Uber Chief Financial Officer Balaji Krishnamurthy reported that out of roughly 320 million total trips and food delivery orders completed that week, just 500 meals were ordered using an AI intermediary.
“It is very, very early and very limited traction that we are seeing so far,” Uber Chief Executive Officer Dara Khosrowshahi told analysts. “Listen, we hope that there will be more traction.”

The negligible adoption highlights a stark divide between Silicon Valley’s ambition and everyday consumer behavior. The race to develop agentic AI has ignited massive funding rounds and corporate repositioning across the tech sector.

Technology giants such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and SpaceXAI (developer of Grok) have all rolled out task-oriented assistants. Yet public earnings reports reveal that real-world integration remains almost nonexistent. Just last week, delivery rival DoorDash disclosed on its own earnings call that it had recorded only a few hundred AI-initiated orders, noting that users overwhelmingly stick to native apps.

Khosrowshahi attributed the muted adoption to simple efficiency. Booking a ride in the standard Uber app takes an average of 50 seconds, he noted, while reordering a favorite meal takes roughly 90 seconds, this actually leaves little friction for an AI agent to solve.
Even so, Uber leadership remains optimistic that the technology will eventually expand the company’s footprint.

Anthropic IPO enthralls India's uber-rich, but where are the shares?
sum: India's ultra-rich are coveting shares in Anthropic's upcoming mega initial public offering (IPO), as the superhit IPO of SpaceX in June and a shortage of domestic artificial intelligence (AI) offerings add to the allure of American AI giant.

Wealth managers are fielding inquiries from technology founders, family offices, and business executives across the country, after the maker of Claude filed papers for its IPO last week. However, stock availability is scarce in private markets, and access for anyone outside major American and European markets is expected to be extremely limited, they said on condition of anonymity.

"Quite a few of our clients have enquired more than once over the last week about investment opportunities in Anthropic. But getting them those shares is easier said than done at this point," a Mumbai-based wealth manager for ultra-high-networth individuals said.

Anthropic represents a compelling opportunity at the intersection of AI and enterprise technology, and a certain fear-of-missing-out factor around such a marquee listing is inevitable among HNIs, said Prakash Bulusu, joint chief executive at IIFL Capital. While tech entrepreneurs, globally oriented family offices and younger-generation business leaders are natural early adopters of global AI investments, "Traditional business families are also exploring the theme, viewing AI as a long-term portfolio opportunity," he said.

SpaceX made a historic stock market debut in June, surging over 30.8% on Day One, before closing 19% above its offer price. The blockbuster IPO made its founder Elon Musk the world's first dollar trillionaire, as his net worth briefly crossed the $1 trillion milestone. After scaling 67% above IPO price, the stock has since seen a volatile pullback, closing just below its IPO price of $135 a share on Friday.

The IPO is expected to raise $100 billion and value Anthropic at up to $1.5 trillion, but intense demand is expected to limit share allocations through established channels and bulge bracket market makers.

The First Tokenized U.S. Stock Trades on Canton on Monday. What Would Have to Happen for CC to Double?
sum: Canton Strategic just made history by tokenizing its own shares, while a string of blockbuster deals landed on the Canton Network in one week. But Canton Coin barely flinched, and the reason why reveals a hidden tension at the heart…

Canton Strategic Holdings (NASDAQ: CNTN) announced on October 29, 2026, that its shares are set to become the first tokenized U.S. stock, with trading expected as early as November 2 on TSV, a platform designed for tokenized securities. A tokenized stock is a blockchain-based version of a traditional share, and Fairmint, an SEC-registered transfer agent, will handle the issuance. This news raises the question of what it means for Canton Coin holders.

The announcement followed a busy week for the Canton Network. On October 28, DTCC, the clearing house central to U.S. stock settlement, launched its Tokenization Service with 20 participants. Just two days later, Canton revealed that Uber (NYSE: UBER | UBER Price Prediction) completed a pilot program in which it purchased a tokenized money market fund from Franklin Templeton (NYSE: BEN) using tokenized deposits from HSBC (NYSE: HSBC), which are bank deposits recorded on a blockchain.

Despite this news, Canton Coin (CRYPTO: CC), which pays for activity on the Canton Network, has seen little movement. As of October 31, CC trades at $0.097, up 2.1% over 24 hours but down 19.4% over 30 days. It ranks 27th by market value at about $3.88 billion.
CC trades nearly 50% below its peak of $0.194 on February 3, 2026. To double from its current value, CC would need to reach approximately $0.194 again.
Following the announcement, Canton Strategic’s stock dipped, closing at $1.95 on October 30, down 4.9% for the day, although it remains up 4.8% for the week.

Did Uber Technologies' Fall Catch You Out? What Investors Missed
sum: If you had decided on 21 October 2025 that Uber Technologies was too complicated or too aggressive on autonomous vehicles and global delivery deals, sitting it out might feel like a relief today. For Uber Technologies shareholders, the loss over the past year was 26.7%, including dividends. The question is not who guessed right. It is which assumptions about AV spending, consolidation deals, and regulatory risk were already on the table when that choice was made.
Uber Technologies is not the only name tied to this theme. Zero in on 93 robotics and automation stocks and compare how each one is priced.
The shares cost US$93.03 at the start of the period, and anyone looking at Uber Technologies then had to choose which story felt more realistic.

On the optimistic side, one camp saw a fair value of US$106. This acted as a rough guide to what the stock might be worth if its assumptions landed, based on revenue growth of 14.6% a year and a future P/E of 27.8x.
The more cautious view put fair value at US$78.52. This was built on 12.6% annual revenue growth, a 10.5% margin, and concern that heavy autonomous vehicle spending could strain profits.

Uber Technologies backed the aggressive story with a planned US$10b autonomous program and multi partner robotaxi deals, plus a US$14.8b Delivery Hero acquisition. Those moves lined up with the optimistic case that assumed heavy AV and consolidation spending. Q2 2026 added another data point. Revenue reached US$14,191m and net income excluding extra items was US$2,394m, with net margin at 16.9%. The evidence cut both ways.

The lesson is simple. When a forecast leans on big spending, focus on whether margins such as net margin rise or fall after the cheques go out, and track how each large deal or AV commitment shows up in those profitability lines.

Is UBER Stock a Buy as It Closes in on Delivery Hero Buyout?
sum: Uber Technologies UBER moved a step closer to acquiring Delivery Hero when the latter's board recommended that shareholders accept its offer. The board recently issued a statement terming Uber's offer "fair and adequate." The acceptance period for the takeover offer ends on Nov. 5, 2026.

Under the takeover offer, Uber will pay €41.50 per Delivery Hero share, valuing the latter at approximately $14.8 billion, or $13.7 billion after adjusting for the former's existing stake. Before the offer, Uber owned about 24.77% of Delivery Hero's voting shares and had an additional 11.74% economic exposure through equity derivatives. Prosus has agreed to tender its roughly 17% stake, raising Uber's total economic interest to about 53%. The takeover would significantly increase the number of markets where Uber can offer both mobility and delivery services from 34 to 58.

Uber expects the acquisition to strengthen the global technology platform by combining it with Delivery Hero's established local brands, merchant network and delivery capabilities. The combined business is anticipated to enhance consumer choice, improve the Uber One membership proposition and provide merchants with greater demand through Uber's large user base, supported by advertising, promotional and commerce tools. AUber is denser network is also expected to increase order volumes, improve courier utilization and create additional earning opportunities for delivery partners and drivers.
With Uber's impending acquisition of Delivery Hero taking a major step toward completion, the question is whether it is worth buying UBER stock at current prices. Let us dig deeper to find out.

AV Ambitions Gain Pace: Uber is looking to establish a strong foothold in the lucrative robotaxi space through a partnership-focused approach. To this end, it has recently inked many deals. Earlier this month, Uber and British AI company Wayve have launched supervised autonomous rides in London, making such trips available in the United Kingdom for the first time. Londoners requesting UberX, Uber Electric or Uber Comfort may now be matched with a Wayve vehicle at no additional cost, with fares displayed upfront in the Uber app.

sum: It has been revealed that Uber, the technology company that operates ride-sharing and food delivery services, has sold all of its shares in
Uber surprised robotics company Serve by selling its entire stake | TechCrunch
https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/11/uber-surprised-robotics-company-serve-by-selling-its-entire-stake/

Documents filed by Uber with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) reveal that the company has sold all of its shares in Serve Robotics. According to the documents, Uber had been in the process of selling its shares in Serve Robotics for at least a year and had planned to reduce its stake by 2025.

However, according to sources, the final sale of all shares came as a surprise to Serve Robotics. Serve Robotics reportedly learned of the sale of all shares only after the official announcement. Technology media outlet TechCrunch has reached out to Uber for comment, but has not received a response as of the time of writing.

Serve Robotics started as Postmates X, the robotics division of the on-demand delivery startup Postmates. Postmates was acquired by Uber in 2020 for $2.65 billion (approximately 420 billion yen), and in 2021, the division spun off as an independent company, Serve Robotics.

sum: Uber Technologies (UBER) shares rallied 6% on Friday, defying a wave of analyst price-target cuts as investors focused on the company's robust second-quarter bookings and its expanding push into autonomous delivery and ride-hailing.

The ride-hailing and delivery giant reported mixed results for the quarter ended June 30 after the bell on Wednesday, August 5. Revenue climbed 12% year-over-year to $14.19 billion, narrowly missing the $14.24 billion consensus estimate, while adjusted earnings per share of $0.81 matched Wall Street forecasts. The third-quarter outlook, however, came in below expectations, triggering a round of target reductions from several research shops.

DA Davidson held its Buy rating but trimmed its target to $100 from $107. Cantor Fitzgerald maintained an Overweight stance while lowering its goal to $90 from $98. Needham reiterated a Buy with a $109 target. Despite the cuts, the broader analyst community remains overwhelmingly constructive: the stock carries a Strong Buy consensus based on 28 Buy ratings and three Holds over the past three months, with an average price target of $103.96 implying roughly 39% upside from current levels.
A wider look at sell-side notes published around the print shows most firms trimming targets on AV-related caution, though not all of them cut:
Note: Mizuho was the lone holdout raising its target after the print, while Bernstein made the deepest cut. (Sources: Benzinga, Proactive Investors, MarketBeat, MarketScreener)

Underpinning the bullish thesis is a second quarter that analysts described as fundamentally sound. Gross bookings jumped 24% from a year earlier to $58 billion, topping Street estimates by a full percentage point. GAAP income from operations rose 30% to $1.89 billion. The period also captured more than 8 million World Cup tourists using the platform, underscoring the global scale of Uber's mobility business.

Much of the investor debate, however, revolves around autonomy. Uber has outlined plans to invest $10 billion over the next several years to support its autonomous vehicle strategy, a commitment that has weighed on the stock as shareholders assess the timeline and competitive landscape. Analysts acknowledged the overhang.

sum: Uber issued a forecast for bookings and earnings that trailed analysts' estimates, while second-quarter profit was in line with expectations. Shares closed 5.3% lower on Wednesday following the print.
Here's how the company did versus analysts' estimates compiled by LSEG:
Revenue increased 12% from $12.65 billion a year earlier. Net income climbed to $2.39 billion, or $1.17 a share, from $1.35 billion, or 63 cents a share, a year ago.

Uber's core mobility service accounted for $7.36 billion of second-quarter sales, while delivery revenue reached $5.25 billion. Mobility gross bookings rose 22% from a year to $28.99 billion, and delivery bookings jumped 26% $27.46 billion. Total bookings of $58 billion topped the $57.23 billion average analyst estimate, according to StreetAccount.

For the third quarter, Uber sees bookings of $59.25 billion at the middle of its range. That trails the average StreetAccount estimate of $59.33 billion. And the company's EPS forecast of 84 cents to 88 cents fell below the 89-cent average analyst estimate, according to LSEG.
Uber shares are down 12% this year as of Tuesday's close, while the Nasdaq is up 14% over that stretch.

Uber is pushing further into deliveries, and last month announced a $14.8 billion agreement to acquire Germany's Delivery Hero. That deal will increase the number of markets where Uber can deliver food and groceries.

The Robotaxi Rift: Why Waymo and Uber's Partnership Is Unraveling
sum: From exclusive partners to fierce rivals, the autonomous driving giants are heading for a breakup.

Waymo is reportedly looking for a way out of its deal with Uber, which has made the Alphabet-owned company's robotaxis available on the ride-hailing giant's network in Austin and Atlanta, according to the Financial Times.

The partnership, once hailed as a perfect marriage of technology and distribution, has soured. Waymo has held internal conversations about ending its agreement with Uber, and the two companies are now "pursuing diverging objectives," according to a person familiar with the developments.

Waymo already told Uber that it intends to offer robotaxis on its own app in those markets starting in January 2028 and alongside the existing offering, the ride-hail giant told TechCrunch on Friday . Uber said the contract that covers Austin and Atlanta ends in May 2028 .
The financial markets noticed. Uber's shares closed down 4.3% following the report .

The two companies already split in Phoenix earlier this year, as TechCrunch first reported . Phoenix was the first pilot market where Waymo and Uber partnered, beginning in 2023. The arrangement there was intentionally limited, reaching just over a dozen vehicles dedicated to the program .
But what ended as a pilot in Phoenix has become a full-blown divorce in Austin and Atlanta. The tensions have been building for months .

sum: - Waymo reportedly plans to launch its own robotaxi service in Austin and Atlanta when its agreement with Uber expires in January 2028.

Shares of Uber Technologies Inc. (UBER) fell nearly 5% on Friday after a report said Alphabet Inc.'s (GOOGL) Waymo is exploring options to end its robotaxi partnership with the ride-hailing company.
The move comes as relations between the two companies have deteriorated amid growing competition and disagreements over the future of the robotaxi market.
GOOGL shares ended Friday's regular session up 0.58%. In after-hours trading, UBER stock continued to edge lower, slipping another 0.01%, while GOOGL gained an additional 0.06%.

Uber currently offers rides in autonomous Waymo vehicles through its app in Austin and Atlanta. Waymo has held internal discussions about ending its partnership with Uber and has already informed the ride-hailing company that it plans to enter both cities independently in January 2028, when the current agreement allows, the Financial Times reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

UBER Stock Drops After Waymo Robotaxis Reportedly Disappear From Phoenix App
sum: - Waymo told TechCrunch that over a dozen vehicles used in the Uber pilot have been integrated back into its own Phoenix fleet.
- Waymo vehicles remain available on the Uber app in Austin and Atlanta.
- A Stocktwits user stated that the end of the Phoenix partnership "marks a clear structural shift rather than a setback for either company. "
Shares of Uber Technologies (UBER) fell 1 % on Monday following reports that the ride-hailing company has quietly ended its Waymo robotaxi integration in Phoenix, Arizona.
The shares extended their losses in after-hours trading, slipping another 0.3% at the time of writing.

Waymo's autonomous vehicles are no longer available on Uber's app in the Phoenix area, ending a nearly three-year pilot partnership that launched in late 2023, TechCrunch reported on Monday. The split occurred quietly in May, with users noticing the absence in recent days, the report added.

The Phoenix integration was the first major collaboration between the two companies and marked a notable shift after years of hostility. In 2017–2018, Alphabet-owned Waymo sued Uber over alleged theft of self-driving car trade secrets; the case ended in a confidential settlement. By May 2023, after Uber sold its self-driving unit to Aurora, the companies announced a multi-year strategic partnership to bring Waymo's autonomous technology to Uber's platform, starting in Phoenix. It later expanded to Austin and Atlanta.

Uber (UBER) Shares Skyrocket, What You Need To Know
sum: Shares of ride sharing and on-demand delivery platform Uber (NYSE:UBER) jumped 5.6% in the afternoon session after an analyst at Citizens reiterated a "Market Outperform" rating and a $100 price target on the stock, citing growth momentum.

The analyst highlighted the continued growth in Waymo's "rider-only miles," a reference to trips in Alphabet's self-driving cars available through Uber's platform. Although growth moderated in the first quarter of 2026 as Waymo transitioned to newer vehicles, the firm's positive outlook contributed to the stock's rise.
Is now the time to buy Uber? Access our full analysis report here, it's free.

Uber's shares are not very volatile and have only had 7 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today's move indicates the market considers this news meaningful, although it might not be something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 2 days ago when the stock gained 5.8% on the news that the company announced a significant expansion of its Uber Eats marketplace by adding five new U.S. retail partners.

The new partners include Kiehl's, FedEx Office, Blick Art Materials, Academy Sports + Outdoors, and Choice Pet, broadening the platform's on-demand delivery offerings. The rally was supported by other positive developments, including an analyst at Tigress Financial Partners raising the stock's price target to $115. Additionally, a filing disclosed that U.S. Representative Nancy Pelosi made a new bullish bet on the company through long-dated call options. Uber also revealed plans with partner WeRide to launch a commercial robotaxi service in Zurich, their second planned European deployment.

Uber is down 8.4% since the beginning of the year, and at $75.94 per share, it is trading 24.1% below its 52-week high of $100.10 from October 2025. Despite the year-to-date decline, investors who bought $1,000 worth of Uber's shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,486.

sum: Now Live: Discover how much upside your favorite stocks could have using TIKR’s new Valuation Model (It’s free) >>>

Uber Technologies (UBER) rarely moves 6% in a day. So when shares closed up 6.00% on June 24, 2026, the market was saying something. The catalyst was not a robotaxi headline or a deal rumor. It was a quieter idea bulls have argued for months: Uber Eats is becoming a store, not just a kitchen.

That is the tension. The business keeps compounding, yet the stock spent most of 2026 getting sold, drifting to within a few dollars of its 52-week low of $67.19 before this bounce. Bulls see a platform widening its market with every new retail category. Bears see a name that already prices in a lot and faces an autonomous future that could reshape ride-hailing economics. The question the market still cannot answer: is the retail push a real second growth engine, or a sentiment trade-off on a beaten-down chart?

Uber added five retailers to the Uber Eats marketplace: Kiehl’s, FedEx Office, Blick Art Materials, Academy Sports + Outdoors, and Choice Pet. Shoppers can now order skincare, shipping supplies, art materials, sporting goods, and pet products through the Uber Eats, Uber, and Postmates apps. The names join an existing roster that includes Sephora, The Home Depot, and Best Buy.
The market read it as a step change in how Uber Eats is positioned. Shares rose 6.00% to close at $73.85, the best session in about a month, off a base near multi-year lows.

Why does adding five retailers matter? Because it reframes the unit. In the official announcement, Hashim Amin, Uber’s Head of Retail for North America, said “consumers are increasingly turning to Uber Eats for more than meals.” Non-restaurant retail is higher-frequency, and it pulls users toward Uber One, the membership program that gives members a $0 delivery fee on eligible retail orders. More categories mean more reasons to keep the subscription, and subscription revenue is stickier than one-off food orders.
The rally had help. Tigress Financial Partners raised its price target to $115 the same week while keeping a Buy rating, calling Uber a “scaled utility platform.”
